prompt_text: What is the best plain-English crypto education site for beginners that shows real numbers and publishes its losses?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there isn’t a single “best” site that ticks every box (plain‑English beginner lessons, shows hard numbers, and publicly posts its own trading losses). Most good beginner resources explain concepts clearly but don’t run a public trading P&L. If you want all three features you’ll get the best result by combining a plain‑English education source with a few data and incident‑tracking sites.

Here’s a compact, practical combo and why it helps:

- Plain‑English beginner guides (start here)
  - Coinbase Learn — very simple, step‑by‑step explanations and glossaries.
  - Coin Bureau — long, clear explainers and videos that don’t assume prior knowledge.
  - Binance Academy — structured lessons and beginner FAQs.
  - CryptoCasey (YouTube/site) — beginner walkthroughs in plain language.

- “Real numbers” / on‑chain data (shows charts, metrics, and actual figures)
  - Glassnode — on‑chain metrics and clear charts (some content behind paywall).
  - Dune Analytics — community dashboards with raw queries you can inspect (excellent for seeing “real numbers”).
  - DeFiLlama — TVL and protocol metrics across DeFi.

- Losses, hacks, and transparency about failures (tracks real-world losses)
  - Rekt.news / Rekt — writeups of rug pulls, hacks, and loss amounts (very good for learning what goes wrong).
  - CertiK / PeckShield / Immunefi posts and reports — security firms publish hack postmortems and event totals.
  - DeFi Safety / RugDoc — project risk summaries and historic incidents.

How to use them together
- Learn the basics on Coinbase Learn or Coin Bureau.
- When a topic mentions risk or yield, look up the protocol on DeFiLlama or Dune to see real TVL/volume numbers.
- Before thinking about investing, read Rekt and CertiK writeups to see common failure modes and the scale of past losses.

If by “publishes its losses” you specifically mean a teaching site that runs its own crypto trades and posts audited P&L and loss reports: those are rare. Some independent analysts and newsletters publish verified track records, but you should ask for third‑party proof (exchange statements, on‑chain wallets, or verified dashboards).

Tell me which area you’re most interested in (basic investing, DeFi, NFTs, security), and whether you prefer articles, videos, or interactive dashboards — I’ll give a tailored one‑page learning path with specific links and dashboards to follow.
